task.title: Testing plug-ins with Gradle
task.shortdesc: The Gradle plugin provides tasks that download DITA-OT, install plug-ins, validate DITA content, run transformations and check links. A build can chain these tasks, so that one command tests a plug-in in a clean DITA-OT installation.

ul.li: Java 17 or later, which the Gradle wrapper in this example (Gradle 9) requires.
You do not need to install Gradle or DITA-OT. The downloads Gradle, and the build downloads DITA-OT.

context.p: This scenario builds a small plug-in (com.example.sample-html5) that adds the sample-html5 transformation type, an HTML5 transformation with a custom stylesheet. It then adds a Gradle build that tests the plug-in.
Two kinds of plug-in are involved, and their names are similar:

ul.li: The DITA-OT plug-in is the code you are developing. DITA-OT installs and runs it.
The Gradle plugin (io.github.jyjeanne.dita-ot-gradle) adds DITA-OT task types to Gradle. It only runs in the build, and it is not part of the DITA-OT plug-in.

context.note: The Gradle plugin is an open-source project (Apache License 2.0) that is maintained outside the DITA-OT project. It is published on the . This example uses version 2.8.8. The build script for the DITA-OT documentation also uses this Gradle plugin.

step.cmd: Create a project directory named dita-ot-gradle-plugin, and add a plug-in configuration file (plugin.xml) that declares the new transformation type.

stepxmp.p: The plug-in extends the default HTML5 transformation, so the require element declares org.dita.html5 as a dependency.

step.cmd: Add the Ant script (build_sample-html5.xml) that defines the transformation type, and a css/sample.css stylesheet.

stepxmp.p: The script sets the same four CSS parameters as the plug-in in .

step.cmd: Add test content in a test-content subdirectory.

stepxmp.p: The topics in test-content/topics contain a cross-reference, so that the link check has something to check. For a real plug-in, add content for each feature that the plug-in handles.

step.cmd: Add the Gradle wrapper and a settings.gradle.kts file that names the project.

info.p: Copy gradlew, gradlew.bat and the gradle/wrapper directory from the sample, or, if Gradle is installed, generate them with gradle wrapper.

step.cmd: Add a build script (build.gradle.kts) that applies the Gradle plugin and registers the tasks that test the plug-in.

stepxmp.p: The build script registers these tasks:

strow.stentry: Downloads the DITA-OT version given by the ditaOtVersion property and extracts it to build/dita-ot/dita-ot-version.
Packages the plug-in files, and only those files, as build/plugin/com.example.sample-html5.zip.
Installs the ZIP file into the downloaded DITA-OT. The force property replaces an installation left by an earlier build.
Validates the test content with the downloaded DITA-OT, without running a full transformation.
Checks the links in the test content and fails the build if a link is broken. It reads the source files and does not need DITA-OT.
Transforms the test content with the sample-html5 transformation type that the plug-in installs.
Runs all of the tasks above in dependency order.

stepxmp.p: The task names come from the build script. Only the task types come from the Gradle plugin, which also registers a default task named dita of type DitaOtTask. For the properties of each task type, see .

step.cmd: From the project directory, run the dev task.

info.p: To test against another DITA-OT version, add -PditaOtVersion=version, for example ./gradlew dev -PditaOtVersion=4.2.3.
info.note: With version 2.8.8 of the Gradle plugin on Windows, the plug-in installation fails if the path of the project directory contains spaces. Move the project to a path without spaces, or map it to a drive letter with the subst command and run the build from that drive.

stepresult.p: Gradle validates the test content, checks its links, packages and installs the plug-in, and runs the transformation. Downloaded DITA-OT archives are cached in the .dita-ot/cache directory in your home directory. A DITA-OT version that is already extracted is not downloaded again.

result.note: The files for this sample project are included in the DITA-OT installation directory under docsrc/samples/dita-ot-gradle-plugin/ and on GitHub.
result.p: The generated HTML5 output is in build/output/sample-html5-version, with the sample stylesheet in its css subdirectory. The project has the following layout:
result.codeblock: dita-ot-gradle-plugin ├── build.gradle.kts ├── build_sample-html5.xml ├── ci │ └── dita-ot-matrix.yml ├── css │ └── sample.css ├── gradle │ └── wrapper │ ├── gradle-wrapper.jar │ └── gradle-wrapper.properties ├── gradle.properties ├── gradlew ├── gradlew.bat ├── plugin.xml ├── settings.gradle.kts └── test-content ├── sample.ditamap └── topics ├── intro.dita └── usage.dita

postreq.p: To run the same tests for each DITA-OT version that your plug-in supports, see .
